claim: Homologous recombination (HR)-mediated repair of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) is restricted to the post-replicative phases of the cell cycle.
source: Homologous recombination (HR)-mediated repair of DNA double-strand break (DSB)s is restricted to the post-replicative phases of the cell cycle.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about HR regulation.

claim: Initiation of HR in the G1 phase blocks non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) impairing DSB repair.
source: Initiation of HR in the G1 phase blocks non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) impairing DSB repair.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Completion of HR in G1 cells can lead to the loss-of-heterozygosity (LOH), which is potentially carcinogenic.
source: Completion of HR in G1 cells can lead to the loss-of-heterozygosity (LOH), which is potentially carcinogenic.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a consequence of HR in G1 phase.

claim: miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* specifically suppress the HR-pathway in the G1 phase.
source: We conducted a gain-of-function screen to identify miRNAs that regulate HR-mediated DSB repair, and of these miRNAs, miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* specifically suppress the HR-pathway in the G1 phase.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* target the transcripts of BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51.
source: These miRNAs target the transcripts of HR factors, BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51, and inhibiting miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* increases expression of BRCA1/BRCA2/RAD51 specifically in the G1-phase leading to impaired DSB repair.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by multiple experimental assays including luciferase reporter assays and immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: Inhibiting miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* increases expression of BRCA1/BRCA2/RAD51 specifically in the G1-phase leading to impaired DSB repair.
source: These miRNAs target the transcripts of HR factors, BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51, and inhibiting miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* increases expression of BRCA1/BRCA2/RAD51 specifically in the G1-phase leading to impaired DSB repair.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 5 showing increased expression in G1 phase and increased γ-H2AX foci.

claim: Depletion of CtIP rescues the impaired DSB repair phenotype caused by inhibiting miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b*.
source: Depletion of CtIP, a BRCA1-associated DNA end resection protein, rescues this phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 6 showing rescue of γ-H2AX foci upon CtIP depletion.

claim: Deletion of miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* in independent cohorts of ovarian tumors correlates with significant increase in LOH events/chromosomal aberrations.
source: Furthermore, deletion of miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* in independent cohorts of ovarian tumors correlates with significant increase in LOH events/chromosomal aberrations and BRCA1 expression.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by analysis of TCGA and DF/HCC cohort data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Deletion of miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* in independent cohorts of ovarian tumors correlates with increased BRCA1 expression.
source: Furthermore, deletion of miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* in independent cohorts of ovarian tumors correlates with significant increase in LOH events/chromosomal aberrations and BRCA1 expression.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 7E showing increased BRCA1 expression in tumors with miRNA deletions.

claim: HR requires an undamaged homologous DNA template to replace an adjacent damaged one with high fidelity.
source: HR requires an undamaged homologous DNA template to replace an adjacent damaged one with high fidelity (San Filippo et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: The untemplated NHEJ pathway is more error-prone as it rapidly processes and joins broken DNA ends.
source: By contrast, the untemplated NHEJ pathway is more error-prone as it rapidly processes and joins broken DNA ends (Lieber, 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: HR is restricted to the S/G2 phase and NHEJ is pre-dominant in G1 but has moderate activity throughout the cell cycle.
source: There is tight regulation of the DSB repair pathways during the cell cycle as HR is restricted to the S/G2 phase and NHEJ is pre-dominant in G1 but has moderate activity throughout the cell cycle.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about cell cycle regulation of DSB repair.

claim: The balance of HR and NHEJ proteins (such as BRCA1 and 53BP1) involved in early steps of the two repair pathways are critical for pathway choice and the cell-cycle phase specific regulation of each pathway.
source: The balance of HR and NHEJ proteins (such as BRCA1 and 53BP1) involved in early steps of the two repair pathways are critical for pathway choice and the cell-cycle phase specific regulation of each pathway (Bouwman et al., 2010; Bunting et al., 2010; Chapman et al., 2012b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Initiation of HR via resection of broken DNA ends blocks NHEJ and could lead to unrepaired DSBs in G1 cells.
source: Initiation of HR via resection of broken DNA ends blocks NHEJ and could lead to unrepaired DSBs in G1 cells (Helmink et al., 2011; Escribano-Diaz et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: The physiological consequence of HR-mediated repair of a DSB in the G1-phase is the loss of heterozygosity (LOH).
source: The physiological consequence of HR-mediated repair of a DSB in the G1-phase is the loss of heterozygosity (LOH).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a consequence of HR in G1 phase.

claim: Ectopic HR leading to LOH may play a critical role in carcinogenesis as recessive oncogenic mutations are revealed and/or tumor suppressor function is lost.
source: Ectopic HR leading to LOH may play a critical role in carcinogenesis as recessive oncogenic mutations are revealed and/or tumor suppressor function is lost (Bishop and Schiestl, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Chemical inhibitors of the DNA repair protein, poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP), exhibit synthetic lethality in BRCA-deficient tumors that have a defective HR pathway.
source: Chemical inhibitors of the DNA repair protein, poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP), exhibit synthetic lethality in BRCA-deficient tumors that have a defective HR pathway (Bryant et al., 2005; Farmer et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Lack of PARP activity in an HR-deficient scenario leads to the accumulation of DSBs in proliferating cells and this triggers apoptosis.
source: Although the molecular mechanism underlying this phenotype remains unresolved, lack of PARP activity in an HR-deficient scenario leads to the accumulation of DSBs in proliferating cells and this triggers apoptosis (Helleday, 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Epigenetic suppression of factors in the HR pathway occurs in sporadic breast and ovarian tumors, and collectively this phenotype has been described as 'BRCAness'.
source: Epigenetic suppression of factors in the HR pathway occurs in sporadic breast and ovarian tumors, and collectively this phenotype has been described as 'BRCAness' (Turner et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Tumors with the 'BRCAness' phenotype are likely to respond to PARP inhibitors.
source: Tumors with the 'BRCAness' phenotype are likely to respond to PARP inhibitors, and identifying factors (such as microRNAs) that induce the 'BRCAness' phenotype may enhance the clinical utility and scope of PARP inhibitors.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a rationale for the study.

claim: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are abundant small (∼20–22 nts) non-coding RNAs that typically dampen gene expression at the post-transcriptional level.
source: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are abundant small (∼20–22 nts) non-coding RNAs that typically dampen gene expression at the post-transcriptional level (Fabian et al., 2010) and are aberrantly expressed in a variety of cancer cells (Garzon et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: miRNAs are aberrantly expressed in a variety of cancer cells.
source: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are abundant small (∼20–22 nts) non-coding RNAs that typically dampen gene expression at the post-transcriptional level (Fabian et al., 2010) and are aberrantly expressed in a variety of cancer cells (Garzon et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: A single miRNA can influence the expression of many mRNAs, and conversely a single mRNA is targeted by multiple miRNAs.
source: The regulation elicited by miRNAs is highly complex, given that a single miRNA can influence the expression of many mRNAs, and conversely a single mRNA is targeted by multiple miRNAs (Bartel, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: miR-182 targets BRCA1.
source: Using the experimental system of in vitro hematopoietic cell differentiation, we discovered that miR-182 targets BRCA1 (Moskwa et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Over-expression of miR-182 in triple negative breast tumor lines suppresses HR via down-regulation of BRCA1 and sensitizes cells to PARP inhibitors.
source: Over-expression of miR-182 in triple negative breast tumor lines (in vitro and in vivo) suppresses HR via down-regulation of BRCA1 and sensitizes cells to PARP inhibitors.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with reference to previous work.

claim: The miRNA mimic libraries from Applied Biosystems and Qiagen impacted ABT888 sensitivity over different ranges.
source: The miRNA mimics from Applied Biosystems impacted ABT888 sensitivity over a broad range, ∼10- to 12-fold difference between the mimics with the highest impact on viability and the control mimics. Whereas the viability range with the mimics from Qiagen was limited to 3- to 4-fold.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the screen results.

claim: The Applied Biosystems library yielded a rank ordered list of the top 13 miRNAs (including miR-182) based on viability percentage that sensitized cells to ABT888.
source: The Applied Biosystems library yielded a rank ordered list of the top 13 miRNAs (including miR-182) based on viability percentage that sensitized cells to ABT888 (Figure 1C) (Z-score thresholds [Z < −2]).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 1C showing the list of miRNAs.

claim: 12 of the 13 miRNAs from the Applied Biosystems screen had at least a 25% impact on ABT888 sensitivity when tested with the Qiagen library.
source: Our results show that 12 of the 13 miRNAs had at least a 25% impact on ABT888 sensitivity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as validation of the primary screen.

claim: 11 of the 12 miRNAs significantly diminished HR-mediated DSB repair.
source: Using this assay, 11 of the 12 miRNAs significantly diminished HR-mediated DSB repair, which correlated with their impact on PARPi sensitivity. (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2A,B showing the DR-GFP assay results.

claim: Over-expression of 7 miRNAs (miR-1231, miR-1255b, miR-148b*, miR-876-3p, miR-221*, miR-193b*, and miR-185*) in MDA-MB231 cells had a significant impact on RAD51 foci ranging from a 50–75% reduction in foci formation.
source: Consistent with our DR-GFP reporter assay, over-expression of all 7 miRNAs in MDA-MB231 cells had a significant impact on RAD51 foci ranging from a 50–75% reduction in foci formation (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2C showing RAD51 foci quantification.

claim: Transfection of mimics for the 7 miRNAs that impacted HR increased γ-H2AX levels 12 hr after treatment with ABT888 and this was maintained through 24 hr.
source: Transfection of mimics for the 7 miRNAs that impacted HR increased γ-H2AX levels 12 hr after treatment with ABT888 and this was maintained through 24 hr.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 2D showing γ-H2AX accumulation.

claim: Of the seven miRNAs, only miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* had detectable and aberrant over expression in TNBC lines.
source: Of these seven miRNAs, only miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* had detectable and aberrant over expression in TNBC lines (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3A showing miRNA expression in breast cancer lines.

claim: Over-expressing miR-1255b reduces the cellular levels of BRCA1 and BRCA2.
source: Over-expressing miR-1255b reduces the cellular levels of BRCA1 and BRCA2, miR-148b* reduces RAD51 and miR-193b* reduces BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 (Figure 3C), and this impact is not related to an altered cell cycle (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3C showing immunoblot results.

claim: Over-expressing miR-148b* reduces RAD51.
source: Over-expressing miR-1255b reduces the cellular levels of BRCA1 and BRCA2, miR-148b* reduces RAD51 and miR-193b* reduces BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 (Figure 3C), and this impact is not related to an altered cell cycle (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3C showing immunoblot results.

claim: Over-expressing miR-193b* reduces BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51.
source: Over-expressing miR-1255b reduces the cellular levels of BRCA1 and BRCA2, miR-148b* reduces RAD51 and miR-193b* reduces BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 (Figure 3C), and this impact is not related to an altered cell cycle (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3C showing immunoblot results.

claim: miR-1255b selectively pulled-down BRCA1 and BRCA2 transcripts but not the RAD51 transcript.
source: Strikingly, consistent with our previous results, miR-1255b selectively pulled-down BRCA1 and BRCA2 transcripts but not the RAD51 transcript (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3F showing immunoprecipitation results.

claim: miR-148b* pulled-down RAD51 transcript but not BRCA1 and BRCA2 transcripts.
source: Conversely, miR-148b* pulled-down RAD51 transcript but not BRCA1 and BRCA2 transcripts, and miR-193b* pulled down all three transcripts.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3F showing immunoprecipitation results.

claim: miR-193b* pulled down BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 transcripts.
source: Conversely, miR-148b* pulled-down RAD51 transcript but not BRCA1 and BRCA2 transcripts, and miR-193b* pulled down all three transcripts.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3F showing immunoprecipitation results.

claim: The miR-1255b/miR-193b* combination immunoprecipitated increased the amount of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mRNAs.
source: Relative to the individual counterparts, the miR-1255b/miR-193b*combination immunoprecipitated increased the amount of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mRNAs and the miR-148b*/miR-193b* combination immunoprecipitated increased RAD51 mRNA (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3G showing immunoprecipitation results with combined mimics.

claim: The miR-148b*/miR-193b* combination immunoprecipitated increased RAD51 mRNA.
source: Relative to the individual counterparts, the miR-1255b/miR-193b*combination immunoprecipitated increased the amount of BRCA1 and BRCA2 mRNAs and the miR-148b*/miR-193b* combination immunoprecipitated increased RAD51 mRNA (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 3G showing immunoprecipitation results with combined mimics.

claim: None of the three transcripts BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 had MREs with a canonical seed region in the 3′UTR for miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b*.
source: None of the three transcripts BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 had MREs with a canonical seed region in the 3′UTR for miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b*.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the MRE analysis.

claim: There were putative non-canonical MREs for miR-193b*, miR-1255b, and miR-148b* in the transcripts of BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51.
source: Using this approach, we observed that consistent with our experimental data, there were putative non-canonical MREs for miR-193b*, miR-1255b, and miR-148b* in the transcripts of BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4A showing predicted MREs.

claim: There was significant decrease in luciferase activity when MREs were cloned in the 3′UTR of the luciferase gene in cells transfected with mimics for miR-1255b, miR-193b*, and miR-148b*.
source: As anticipated, there was significant decrease in luciferase activity, and this was 'rescued' by point mutations that disrupt base pairing between miR-1255b, miR-193b*, and miR-148b* and their corresponding MREs in BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4B showing luciferase reporter assay results.

claim: Point mutations that disrupt base pairing between miR-1255b, miR-193b*, and miR-148b* and their corresponding MREs in BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 rescued the decrease in luciferase activity.
source: As anticipated, there was significant decrease in luciferase activity, and this was 'rescued' by point mutations that disrupt base pairing between miR-1255b, miR-193b*, and miR-148b* and their corresponding MREs in BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4B showing luciferase reporter assay results with mutant MREs.

claim: Inhibition of miR-1255b enhanced luciferase activity of the BRCA1 and BRCA2 reporter construct.
source: We estimated luciferase activity after inhibiting the miRNAs using antagomirs and, consistent with our previous results, found that inhibition of miR-1255b enhanced luciferase activity of the BRCA1 and BRCA2 reporter construct, inhibition of miR-148b* enhanced luciferase activity of the RAD51 reporter construct, and inhibition of miR-193b* enhanced luciferase activity of the BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 reporter constructs (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4D showing luciferase reporter assay results with antagomirs.

claim: Inhibition of miR-148b* enhanced luciferase activity of the RAD51 reporter construct.
source: We estimated luciferase activity after inhibiting the miRNAs using antagomirs and, consistent with our previous results, found that inhibition of miR-1255b enhanced luciferase activity of the BRCA1 and BRCA2 reporter construct, inhibition of miR-148b* enhanced luciferase activity of the RAD51 reporter construct, and inhibition of miR-193b* enhanced luciferase activity of the BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 reporter constructs (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4D showing luciferase reporter assay results with antagomirs.

claim: Inhibition of miR-193b* enhanced luciferase activity of the BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 reporter constructs.
source: We estimated luciferase activity after inhibiting the miRNAs using antagomirs and, consistent with our previous results, found that inhibition of miR-1255b enhanced luciferase activity of the BRCA1 and BRCA2 reporter construct, inhibition of miR-148b* enhanced luciferase activity of the RAD51 reporter construct, and inhibition of miR-193b* enhanced luciferase activity of the BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 reporter constructs (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 4D showing luciferase reporter assay results with antagomirs.

claim: The BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 expression constructs lacking the specific MREs completely restored the expression of these genes in the presence of the corresponding miRNA mimic.
source: First, the BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 expression constructs lacking the specific MREs completely restored the expression of these genes in the presence of the corresponding miRNA mimic further validating the predicted MREs (Figure 5A, lower panel).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5A showing rescue experiments.

claim: Expression of BRCA1 or BRCA2 significantly 'rescued' the impact of miR-1255b on ABT888 sensitivity.
source: Furthermore, in regard to ABT888 sensitivity, expression of BRCA1 or BRCA2 significantly 'rescued' the impact of miR-1255b, expression of BRCA1 or BRCA2 or RAD51 significantly 'rescued' the impact of miR-193b*, and expression of RAD51 significantly 'rescued' the impact of miR-148b* (Figure 5A, upper panel).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5A showing rescue of ABT888 sensitivity.

claim: Expression of BRCA1 or BRCA2 or RAD51 significantly 'rescued' the impact of miR-193b* on ABT888 sensitivity.
source: Furthermore, in regard to ABT888 sensitivity, expression of BRCA1 or BRCA2 significantly 'rescued' the impact of miR-1255b, expression of BRCA1 or BRCA2 or RAD51 significantly 'rescued' the impact of miR-193b*, and expression of RAD51 significantly 'rescued' the impact of miR-148b* (Figure 5A, upper panel).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5A showing rescue of ABT888 sensitivity.

claim: Expression of RAD51 significantly 'rescued' the impact of miR-148b* on ABT888 sensitivity.
source: Furthermore, in regard to ABT888 sensitivity, expression of BRCA1 or BRCA2 significantly 'rescued' the impact of miR-1255b, expression of BRCA1 or BRCA2 or RAD51 significantly 'rescued' the impact of miR-193b*, and expression of RAD51 significantly 'rescued' the impact of miR-148b* (Figure 5A, upper panel).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5A showing rescue of ABT888 sensitivity.

claim: mRNA levels of BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 are enhanced in the S-phase.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Gudas et al., 1996; Vaughn et al., 1996; Chen et al., 1997), we observe that mRNA levels of BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 are enhanced in the S-phase (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and supported by Figure 5B,C showing qRT-PCR results in synchronized cells.

claim: miR-1255b, miR-193b*, and miR-148b* inversely correlate with their target transcripts, and are significantly down-regulated as cells move into the S-phase.
source: miR-1255b, miR-193b*, and miR-148b* inversely correlate with their target transcripts, and are significantly down-regulated as cells move into the S-phase.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5B,C showing miRNA expression in synchronized cells.

claim: Transfection of the miR-1255b ANT causes significant increase in BRCA1 and BRCA2 and not RAD51 in G1 cells.
source: Antagonizing these miRNAs induces a specific increase in target transcripts (Figure 5D) and proteins (Figure 5E) in the G1-phase, that is transfection of the miR-1255b ANT causes significant increase in BRCA1 and BRCA2 and not RAD51, miR-148b* ANT increases RAD51 and miR-193b* ANT increases BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 in G1 cells (Figure 5D,E, cell cycle profiles are shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5D,E showing increased expression in G1 cells.

claim: miR-148b* ANT increases RAD51 in G1 cells.
source: Antagonizing these miRNAs induces a specific increase in target transcripts (Figure 5D) and proteins (Figure 5E) in the G1-phase, that is transfection of the miR-1255b ANT causes significant increase in BRCA1 and BRCA2 and not RAD51, miR-148b* ANT increases RAD51 and miR-193b* ANT increases BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 in G1 cells (Figure 5D,E, cell cycle profiles are shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5D,E showing increased expression in G1 cells.

claim: miR-193b* ANT increases BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 in G1 cells.
source: Antagonizing these miRNAs induces a specific increase in target transcripts (Figure 5D) and proteins (Figure 5E) in the G1-phase, that is transfection of the miR-1255b ANT causes significant increase in BRCA1 and BRCA2 and not RAD51, miR-148b* ANT increases RAD51 and miR-193b* ANT increases BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 in G1 cells (Figure 5D,E, cell cycle profiles are shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5D,E showing increased expression in G1 cells.

claim: Combined inhibition of miRNAs with overlapping targets causes a synergistic increase in target transcripts in G1.
source: Combined inhibition of miRNAs with overlapping targets causes a synergistic increase in target transcripts in G1 (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5F showing synergistic effects.

claim: There is a significant increase in BRCA1 and BRCA2 transcripts in cells co-transfected with miR-1255b ANT and miR-193b*ANT.
source: There is a significant increase in BRCA1 and BRCA2 transcripts in cells co-transfected with miR-1255b ANT and miR-193b*ANT, and a significant increase in RAD51 mRNA in cells co-transfected with miR-148b*ANT and miR-193b*ANT.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5F showing synergistic effects on target transcripts.

claim: There is a significant increase in RAD51 mRNA in cells co-transfected with miR-148b*ANT and miR-193b*ANT.
source: There is a significant increase in BRCA1 and BRCA2 transcripts in cells co-transfected with miR-1255b ANT and miR-193b*ANT, and a significant increase in RAD51 mRNA in cells co-transfected with miR-148b*ANT and miR-193b*ANT.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5F showing synergistic effects on target transcripts.

claim: Loss of NHEJ factors allows the initiation of HR in G1 cells and leads to the persistence of unrepaired DSBs.
source: There is emerging evidence that loss of NHEJ factors allows the initiation of HR in G1 cells and leads to the persistence of unrepaired DSBs (Helmink et al., 2011; Escribano-Diaz et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to support the claim.

claim: Inhibition of miR-1255b and miR-193b* causes a moderate but statistically significant increase in basal γ-H2AX specifically in G1 cells.
source: Inhibition of miR-1255b and miR-193b* causes a moderate but statistically significant increase in basal γ-H2AX specifically in G1 cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6—figure supplement 1A showing γ-H2AX foci in G1 cells.

claim: The impact of inhibiting the miRNAs on DSB repair in G1 cells is more pronounced when these cells are exposed to IR.
source: The impact of inhibiting the miRNAs on DSB repair in G1 cells is even more pronounced when these cells are exposed to IR (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6A,B showing increased γ-H2AX foci after IR.

claim: BRCA1 promotes end resection at DSBs via its interaction with CtIP.
source: BRCA1 promotes end resection at DSBs via its interaction with CtIP (Yun and Hiom, 2009) and that is the key step in blocking NHEJ.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: The significant increase in residual DSBs in cells transfected with antagomirs for miR-1255b, miR-193b* and miR-148b* is 'rescued' by silencing CtIP.
source: The significant increase in residual DSBs in cells transfected with antagomirs for miR-1255b, miR-193b* and miR-148b* is 'rescued' by silencing CtIP (Figure 6A,B; silencing efficacy shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that increased levels of BRCA1 by miRNA inhibition in G1 promotes CtIP-mediated resection.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6A,B showing rescue of γ-H2AX foci upon CtIP depletion.

claim: Increased levels of BRCA1 by miRNA inhibition in G1 promotes CtIP-mediated resection.
source: The significant increase in residual DSBs in cells transfected with antagomirs for miR-1255b, miR-193b* and miR-148b* is 'rescued' by silencing CtIP (Figure 6A,B; silencing efficacy shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that increased levels of BRCA1 by miRNA inhibition in G1 promotes CtIP-mediated resection.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the CtIP rescue experiment.

claim: There is a significant increase in RPA2 foci in the G1 phase of cells transfected with antagomirs for miR-1255b, miR-193b* and miR-148b*.
source: Consistent with resection of DNA ends, and production of ssDNA, we observe a significant increase in RPA2 foci in the G1 phase of cells transfected with antagomirs for miR-1255b, miR-193b* and miR-148b* and again the depletion of CtIP negates the formation of RPA2 foci in these cells (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6C,D showing RPA2 foci quantification.

claim: Depletion of CtIP negates the formation of RPA2 foci in cells transfected with antagomirs for miR-1255b, miR-193b* and miR-148b*.
source: Consistent with resection of DNA ends, and production of ssDNA, we observe a significant increase in RPA2 foci in the G1 phase of cells transfected with antagomirs for miR-1255b, miR-193b* and miR-148b* and again the depletion of CtIP negates the formation of RPA2 foci in these cells (Figure 6C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6C,D showing rescue of RPA2 foci upon CtIP depletion.

claim: Inhibition of miR-1255b, miR-193b*, and miR-148b* in RPE-1 causes a CtIP-dependent increase in residual DSBs in G1 cells.
source: Consistent with the previous results, inhibition of miR-1255b, miR-193b*, and miR-148b* in RPE-1 causes a CtIP-dependent increase in residual DSBs in G1 cells (Figure 6F,G), but this effect is not observed in the S-phase (Figure 6H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6F,G showing γ-H2AX foci in Fucci cells.

claim: The effect of inhibiting miR-1255b, miR-193b*, and miR-148b* on residual DSBs is not observed in the S-phase.
source: Consistent with the previous results, inhibition of miR-1255b, miR-193b*, and miR-148b* in RPE-1 causes a CtIP-dependent increase in residual DSBs in G1 cells (Figure 6F,G), but this effect is not observed in the S-phase (Figure 6H,I).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 6H,I showing no effect in S-phase cells.

claim: The two major mechanisms proposed to cause LOH are deletion of chromosomal fragments/chromosome loss and mitotic recombination between homologous alleles.
source: The two major mechanisms proposed to cause LOH are deletion of chromosomal fragments/chromosome loss and mitotic recombination between homologous alleles (Lasko et al., 1991).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Mitotic recombination is a consequence of HR-mediated repair of DSBs in the G1 phase.
source: Mitotic recombination is a consequence of HR-mediated repair of DSBs in the G1 phase.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference about the mechanism of LOH.

claim: Homologous chromosomes are in close proximity at DSB sites in the G1 phase.
source: Recent studies demonstrate that homologous chromosomes are in close proximity at DSB sites in the G1 phase (Gandhi et al., 2012, 2013) further supporting the notion that HR-mediated DSB repair is feasible in G1 cells and this in turn could lead to LOH.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to support the claim.

claim: There is detectable expression of miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* in a panel of ovarian tumor lines.
source: The HR-pathway and expression of BRCA1 and BRCA2 is extremely relevant in ovarian tumors, and we observed that there is detectable expression of miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* in a panel of ovarian tumor lines (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7A showing miRNA expression in ovarian cancer lines.

claim: The increased γ-H2AX foci correlating with inhibition of miR-1255b, miR-193b*, and miR-148b* is not observed in a BRCA1-mutant ovarian cell line UWB1.289.
source: The increased γ-H2AX foci correlating with inhibition of miR-1255b, miR-193b*, and miR-148b* is not observed in a BRCA1-mutant ovarian cell line UWB1.289 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1) confirming the importance of BRCA1 in the phenotype induced by these miRNAs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7—figure supplement 1 showing no effect in BRCA1-deficient cells.

claim: The number of LOH events is significantly higher in tumors with deletions of miR-148b* and miR-193b* relative to the tumors that are diploid copy neutral at these loci.
source: We observed that the number of LOH events is significantly higher in tumors with deletions of miR-148b* and miR-193b* relative to the tumors that are diploid copy neutral at these loci.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7B showing LOH analysis in TCGA data.

claim: The number of LOH events was moderately higher in tumors with deletion of miR-1225b compared to the copy neutral ones.
source: The number of LOH events was also moderately higher (One tailed Mann Whitney's U test; p<0.08) in tumors with deletion of miR-1225b compared to the copy neutral ones (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7B showing LOH analysis in TCGA data.

claim: Mature miR-1255b is encoded from two distinct genomic loci.
source: It is noteworthy that mature miR-1255b is encoded from two distinct genomic loci (miR-1255b-1 on chr4: 36427988-36428050 and miR-1255b-2 on chr1: 167967898-167967964).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a fact about miR-1255b genomic organization.

claim: There is a significant increase in somatic amplifications and deletions in tumors with deletions in miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b*.
source: Reflecting overall genomic instability, there is a significant increase in somatic amplifications and deletions in tumors with deletions in miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7C showing somatic copy number alterations.

claim: The number of LOH events is higher in the tumors with deletions of miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* relative to the samples that are diploid copy neutral at these loci in the DF/HCC cohort.
source: Consistent with the analysis of the TCGA data, the number of LOH events is higher in the tumors with deletions of miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* relative to the samples that are diploid copy neutral at these loci.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7D showing LOH analysis in DF/HCC cohort.

claim: There is a significant increase in BRCA1 expression in the tumors with deletions in miR-1255b and miR-193b*.
source: Finally, in agreement with our experimental data, there is a significant increase in BRCA1 expression in the tumors with deletions in miR-1255b and miR-193b*(Figure 7E), which we speculate is the underlying reason for the increase in LOH and overall genomic instability.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 7E showing BRCA1 expression analysis.

claim: Increased BRCA1 expression is the underlying reason for the increase in LOH and overall genomic instability in tumors with deletions in miR-1255b and miR-193b*.
source: Finally, in agreement with our experimental data, there is a significant increase in BRCA1 expression in the tumors with deletions in miR-1255b and miR-193b*(Figure 7E), which we speculate is the underlying reason for the increase in LOH and overall genomic instability.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as speculation based on the data.

claim: miRNAs typically target hundreds of transcripts and are more likely to have a profound impact on a pathway like the HR repair pathway by regulating several HR factors.
source: A key conceptual limitation to this approach is that miRNAs typically target hundreds of transcripts and are more likely to have a profound impact on a pathway like the HR repair pathway by regulating several HR factors.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conceptual framework for the study.

claim: Three miRNAs (miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b*) regulate expression of BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51.
source: Here, we systematically identified miRNAs influencing HR (miR-1231, miR-1255b, miR-148b*, miR-876-3p, miR-221*, miR-193b*, and miR-185*) and observed that three of these miRNAs (miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b*) regulate expression of BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion summarizing the main findings.

claim: miR-1255b, miR-148b*, and miR-193b* lack canonical binding sites in the 3′UTR of BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51, but interact with these transcripts via non-canonical MREs.
source: Intriguingly, they lack canonical binding sites in the 3′UTR of BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51, but interact with these transcripts via non-canonical MREs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion summarizing the findings about MREs.

claim: 53BP1 and its associated factors (RIF1 and PTIP) promote NHEJ and counter BRCA1 thereby balancing the process of DSB repair between HR and NHEJ.
source: Specifically 53BP1 and its associated factors (RIF1 and PTIP) promote NHEJ and counter BRCA1 thereby balancing the process of DSB repair between HR and NHEJ (Bouwman et al., 2010; Bunting et al., 2010; Chapman et al., 2012a; Callen et al., 2013; Di Virgilio et al., 2013; Escribano-Diaz et al., 2013; Zimmermann et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to support the claim.

claim: Loss of the 53BP1-associated protein RIF1 or the protein H2AX allows the BRCA1/CtIP-mediated resection of DNA ends in G1 cells impeding NHEJ and leading to the persistence of DNA lesions.
source: Loss of the 53BP1-associated protein RIF1 or the protein H2AX allows the BRCA1/CtIP-mediated resection of DNA ends in G1 cells impeding NHEJ and leading to the persistence of DNA lesions (Helmink et al., 2011; Escribano-Diaz et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with citations to support the claim.

claim: Down-regulating the expression of HR factors, particularly, an HR-initiating factor like BRCA1 in the G1 cells is necessary for maintaining genomic stability.
source: Down-regulating the expression of HR factors, particularly, an HR-initiating factor like BRCA1 in the G1 cells is necessary for maintaining genomic stability.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Inhibiting miR-1255b and miR-193b* allows increased BRCA1 expression in G1 cells leading to CtIP-mediated resection and a potential block in NHEJ.
source: Inhibiting miR-1255b and miR-193b* allows increased BRCA1 expression in G1 cells leading to CtIP-mediated resection and a potential block in NHEJ.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the study.

claim: Execution of HR-mediated repair in G1 cells would result in LOH which has the potential of revealing recessive oncogenic mutations.
source: Furthermore, execution of HR-mediated repair in G1 cells would result in LOH which has the potential of revealing recessive oncogenic mutations.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as an inference about the consequences of HR in G1.

claim: A single copy loss of BRCA1 impacts genomic stability.
source: A single copy loss of BRCA1 (Konishi et al., 2011), BRCA2 (Popova et al., 2012), or RAD51 (Smeenk et al., 2010) impacts genomic stability giving credence to the idea that a miRNA-mediated alteration in the cellular levels of these proteins may significantly impact the DNA repair process.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to support the claim.

evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to support the claim.

evidence: This is stated in the Discussion with a citation to support the claim.

claim: A miRNA-mediated alteration in the cellular levels of BRCA1, BRCA2, or RAD51 may significantly impact the DNA repair process.

claim: The miRNA mimic libraries from Applied Biosystems and Qiagen are based on miRbase 14.
source: miRNA screen was carried out in triplicates using miRNA mimic libraries from Applied Biosystems (Pre-miR miRNA Precursor Library, 885 miRNAs) and Qiagen (miScript miRNA Mimic Library, 875 miRNAs), both the libraries were based on miRbase 14.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the screen.

claim: MDA-MB231 cells were plated at 1000 cells/well density and reverse transfected with 50 nM control miRNA, miRNAs, or BRCA2 siRNA using Lipofectamine RNAiMax transfection reagent.
source: MDA-MB231 cells were plated on 384-well plate at 1000 cells/well density and reverse transfected with 50 nM control miRNA, miRNAs, or BRCA2 siRNA using Lipofectamine RNAiMax transfection reagent before being treated with 20 µM ABT888 next day.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the screen protocol.

claim: The cut off for the miRNA screen was set at 75% control viability and Z-score of positive control, BRCA2 siRNA.
source: % viability control was calculated for each miRNA and the cut off was set at 75% control viability and Z-score of positive control, BRCA2 siRNA.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the screen analysis.
